predecessor.note: Recorded forward-only. No file under contracts/m0 changes — including its manifest, validator, fixtures, and OpenAPI. contracts/validate_schemas.py verifies this hash on every run, and the CI gate additionally runs `git diff --exit-code` over the directory.
predecessor.manifest_sha256_note: Digest of the file with newlines normalised to LF, which is what git stores. The value first recorded here (7b20760b7b9b4be07471ee8b1b79c4aa99c07e257c06425717a1fa9a6fb29c68) was the raw-byte digest of a Windows CRLF checkout, so the check passed on Windows and failed on Linux CI. contracts/m0/SCHEMA_MANIFEST.json itself is unchanged; only this fingerprint of it was wrong.

why_a_package_and_not_an_amendment: D3 REMOVES a required field: readingAssemblyRequest.reading_key. That is squarely inside the M0 breaking_change_policy — 'Any change to required fields, enums, or $id requires a schema_version bump and a new freeze note.'

D1's revision fields would have to be added under readingEvidenceGraph's additionalProperties:false. Additive in intent, still an edit to a frozen schema document, and the amendment precedent in M0 covers OpenAPI only.
Versioning once is cheaper than arguing the boundary twice.

patternlike.cycle-pass-id.v1.note: ADDED additively — see amendments. Keyed on the parent cyc_ rather than on cycleIdentityV1, because oriented_branch and winding never leave the calculation service and the trusted plane that persists a pass therefore cannot rebuild the parent preimage.

cycleHashPreimageV1.rendering: none — generation-command.cyclePin.cycle_hash stores the full 64-character digest
cycleHashPreimageV1.note: ADDED additively — see amendments. Not an identity profile: it names a scan result, not a physical encounter, which is exactly why it carries no identity_profile field and no rendered prefix.

rules: Validated I-JSON values only. Duplicate keys, non-finite numbers, undefined, lone surrogates, and values outside the schema are rejected rather than coerced.
ECMAScript number serialization; recursive UTF-16 property-name ordering; UTF-8 output; no implicit Unicode normalization.
Arrays are put into their contractually defined total order BEFORE canonicalization, because JCS deliberately preserves array order.

The 128-bit rendered suffix is only the opaque handle. Golden vectors retain the full digest AND the exact canonical bytes, so an implementation cannot silently change canonicalization while its digests keep round-tripping.

SCOPE: JCS applies to the patternlike.* profiles listed above and to cycleHashPreimageV1, and to nothing else. M0 release, object, and signature hashes remain byte-frozen on the repository's legacy canonicalJson behaviour (JSON.stringify over sorted keys) — generation-command.release_bundle_hash is recomputed with THAT procedure, not this one. M3 must not reinterpret them as JCS; naming and versioning that legacy profile is still an open escalation.

schemas.note: NEW. M0 pinned output_schema to the literal 'daily-reading-v2' without shipping a document for it, so the assembly identity committed to a schema nobody could validate against. v3 is that document.

ADDED after the freeze, additively — see amendments. generation-command.schema.json required cyclePin.pass_ids and cyclePin.cycle_hash while describing neither preimage, which is the one gap that stops a pass from being persisted at all.

openapi.describes: Public Worker origin — complete successor document, not a fragment.
Calculation service on Fly. Separate so POST /v1/cycles is not falsely advertised on the public Worker origin.

changes_from_m0.summary: A daily reading gets a revision component.
changes_from_m0.detail: reading_key becomes user:<user_id>:<local_date>:<release_version>:r<revision>, which still matches the frozen M0 pattern because its trailing .+ absorbs the suffix. Uniqueness moves off release_version: the M0 key permitted TWO published readings for one user-day whenever a release activated mid-day, against the product's 'one coherent daily chapter'. revision_reason deliberately excludes a content-release reason — activating a release does not retroactively revise published readings.

changes_from_m0.summary: Cycles are a cycle plus an ordered list of passes.
changes_from_m0.detail: The one-pass model made 'reconsidering' unreachable — that state is exactly the interior of a retrograde loop — so the schema could not express the product's own phase vocabulary. Identity is (oriented branch, integer winding), not a pass timestamp, so overlapping scan windows address the same physical encounter.

changes_from_m0.summary: The assembly request carries an opaque assembly_id, never reading_key.
changes_from_m0.detail: Content-addressed, not user-addressed. Not a stable pseudonym either: the preimage carries the day's fact set, so the same user gets an unrelated id each day. Not persisted in a clear column — an unkeyed digest of the exact facts, context, release, and anchor would itself be a dictionary oracle.

changes_from_m0.summary: Version the contract; leave M0 byte-frozen.
Fixture ids resolve against a repo-owned catalogue.
changes_from_m0.detail: fixtures/assembly/<fixture_id>.json. An unknown id is fixtures_unknown, not a pass — otherwise a compromised control plane activates a release by naming fixtures nobody has.

changes_from_m0.summary: daily-reading-v3 is defined rather than merely named.
changes_from_m0.detail: Review correction. The identity preimage pins output_schema, so committing to a schema name with no document behind it puts an unverifiable value inside a hash.
Review correction. M0 made both non-empty and required, which makes the commonest day — no cycle inside orb — unrepresentable, and with it the reviewed universal fallback path such a day must take.

Review correction. The registry requires 'no hidden engagement-only ranking'; leaving resonance_feedback in the vocabulary left the ranker somewhere to record one, with reading_feedback.resonance as the column that would feed it. user_priority is a duplicate of domain_match.

Review correction. Identity creation writes locale 'en-US' as a server default with no writer, exactly as it does for timezone — and M3 makes locale load-bearing for fallback and timing-template selection.

compatibility.breaking_change_policy: Any change to required fields, enums, or $id requires a schema_version bump and a new freeze note. Purely additive changes (a new OpenAPI path, a new inline schema) are recorded in `amendments` instead.
compatibility.wire_format: snake_case on the wire even though TypeScript is camelCase.

out_of_scope_for_this_freeze: Constrained-model editing (M5). assembly_mode stays deterministic; nothing calls a model in M3.
unresolved_escalations: §1 crypto-shredding vs D1 Time Travel: wrapped DEK and ciphertext still share a database. M3 additionally does NOT claim that encrypting reading output makes a reading unrecoverable — see the acceptance note in the M3 plan §5.

§5 cascading revocation: still no derived_features table and no invalidated_at. D1's revision model gives revocation somewhere to land for readings specifically, which is narrower than the general problem.
§8 legacy canonicalJson has no named standard: resolved for the two new patternlike.*-id.v1 profiles only.
§11 snapshot_json precision: unresolved. The cycle scan inherits whatever it settles on rather than inventing a third policy.
§9 techniques_enabled overstates the engine: M3 implements transits, closing one of the declared five. stations_ingresses and lunations_eclipses stay declared-but-absent.

amendments.summary: Four cycle-response fixtures added so every rule in cycle_response_policy() has one.
amendments.detail: Three response-level rules shipped with the freeze had no fixture at all, because every cycle-response fixture carried zero or one cycle: ordering by (exact_at, id), cycle-id uniqueness, and start_at <= end_at. cycle-response.multi.json adds a two-cycle valid twin (the minus branch of the same square, which is a genuinely different encounter and so has a genuinely different id), and cycle-response.unordered-cycles.json, cycle-response.duplicate-cycle-ids.json, and cycle-response.inverted-envelope.json are each one mutation from it. No schema, enum, or $id changed; this does not touch the freeze.

amendments.summary: cycle-derivation.schema.json pins the two derivations the freeze named but never defined: the cyp_ pass-id preimage and the cycle_hash normalization.
amendments.detail: generation-command.schema.json REQUIRES cyclePin.pass_ids and cyclePin.cycle_hash. The freeze specified pass ids only as prose — 'derived from the parent cycle identity plus pass_index' — with no preimage document and no golden vector, and cycle_hash only as a hash 'of the normalized cycle row as scanned' with no stated normalization. Two implementations reading that would mint different ids for the same pass and different hashes for the same scan, and Phase 4 cannot persist a pass until both are pinned. Two decisions are recorded here. First, cyclePassIdentityV1 keys on the parent cyc_ rather than on cycleIdentityV1: oriented_branch and winding are deliberately private to the calculation service and never appear on the wire, so the trusted plane that persists a pass cannot rebuild the parent preimage — and does not need to, because cyc_ is already a collision-resistant function of it. The pass timestamp stays out, because refinement may move exact_at while the index does not move. Second, cycleHashPreimageV1 is the normalized cycle exactly as scanned MINUS importance_score, which is optional and advisory on the wire and cannot change assembly output; including it would fail a claimed job closed over a value that does not affect the reading. No existing $id, required field, or enum changed, so the freeze is untouched.

amendments.summary: content-release.schema.json gains contentReleaseIngestionRequest, the wrapper M0 shipped and this package omitted.
amendments.detail: M0 defines contentReleaseIngestionRequest; M3 redefined contentReleaseBundle but not the request that carries it. The Worker compiles the bundled schemas at startup and had no M3 wrapper to compile, so it was structurally validating M3 ingestion bodies against the M0 bundle — which has no timing_templates, no daily_fallbacks, and a schema_version const of 0.2.0, and therefore rejected every M3 bundle as `/schema_version (const)`. Without this, no release the assembler can read could ever be ingested, and the daily-reading pipeline has no content to assemble from. Identical to the M0 wrapper except that `bundle` points at the M3 bundle. No existing $id, required field, or enum changed.

amendments.summary: Ingestion now enforces the M3 per-locale content rules the OpenAPI already described, and accepts only 0.3.0 bundles.
amendments.detail: openapi.yaml's /internal/content-releases already stated that 'a bundle must carry exactly one universal daily_fallback and at least one default timing_template for every declared supported locale', but the M2 runtime validated neither — it iterated a hardcoded six-collection list that did not include timing_templates or daily_fallbacks, and never read supported_locales. The Worker now validates both new collections, requires supported_locales/locale_default/language_fallbacks to be coherent, checks that every {token} in reviewed timing copy is declared, and enforces the per-locale fallback and default-template rules. It also narrows the accepted schema_version to 0.3.0: a 0.2.0 bundle cannot produce a reading, so accepting one would reserve an immutable release version for bytes that can never be served. Nothing has been ingested in production (CONTENT_RELEASE_KEYS is unset there and ingestion fails closed at 503), so the narrowing orphans no stored release. No contract document changed; this row records that the runtime caught up with one.

amendments.summary: GET /v1/readings/today also answers 409 locale_confirmation_required when the content locale is still the unconfirmed server default.
amendments.detail: openapi.yaml documents only timezone_confirmation_required on this operation's 409; C4's locale writer postdates that wording. buildGenerationCommand withholds generation on EITHER unconfirmed source (apps/api/src/services/generation-command.ts), so a reader with a confirmed zone and a default_unconfirmed locale has no reading and never will until the locale is owned — and the documented 404 reading_not_generated tells that reader to 'check back', which is advice that can never come true. The read route therefore mirrors the generation gate so the answer names the action that unblocks it: PUT /v1/preferences/locale. Timezone is still evaluated first, matching the writer's order. ErrorResponse.error.code carries no enum and 409 was already a documented status on this operation, so no schema, enum, required field, or $id changed; the code was already in the Worker's 409 vocabulary at apps/api/src/routes/internal-generation.ts. The same route also returns details.local_date on the reading_not_generated 404, which ErrorResponse already permits, so a client can name the day it is waiting on rather than say only 'not ready'. This row records that the read surface caught up with the write surface.

amendments.summary: PUT /v1/readings/today can return a closed preparation response while the queue publishes the current local-day reading.
amendments.detail: The existing GET remains read-only. The new body-less PUT is an idempotent desired-state operation whose 200 response reuses dailyReadingResponse and whose 202 response is exactly schema_version, status = preparing, and the server-resolved local_date. Adding one definition, one root-union member, one valid fixture, and one OpenAPI operation changes no existing required field, enum, schema version, or $id and touches no M0 file.
